info.name: fhir-compliance-service (Phase 5 + 5b)
info.description: US Core structural validation + FHIR generation for ClinicalHarmony. Import this into Postman, make sure `docker-compose up -d` is running, and run requests top to bottom. Requests 10+ are Phase 5b: the official HL7 FHIR validator against US Core 6.1.0, and Silver → FHIR → Gold builds (needs docs/db-init/16 and 17 applied). Requests 16-21 are Phase 5b slice 2: C-CDA → FHIR R4 Bundle conversion (POST /api/fhir/convert/ccda), each resource validated against US Core 6.1.0. Requests 22-35 are Phase 5b slice 3: GoldWriter (provisional master patients + data lineage — needs docs/db-init/18 and 19 applied) and the CMS-0057-F payer read API served from Gold (GET /fhir/r4/{Coverage,PractitionerRole,MedicationKnowledge,MeasureReport,Device}). Errors on /fhir/r4 are FHIR OperationOutcomes. seed1_patient / seed2_patient are the FHIR ids of Silver seed patients SEED-0001 / SEED-0002 (silver-patient-<silver.patients.id>).

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, body `{"status":"UP"}`. If this fails, the container isn't running — check `docker ps` for clinicalharmony-fhir-compliance-service.

Expect: 200 OK, a JSON array of 7 rules — one per US Core resource type (USCORE_PATIENT_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_CONDITION_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_OBSERVATION_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_MEDICATIONREQUEST_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_ALLERGYINTOLERANCE_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_ENCOUNTER_COMPLETENESS, USCORE_DIAGNOSTICREPORT_COMPLETENESS). Each has ruleCode, ruleName, category, severity, active, and expression (the requiredFields list).

Expect: 200 OK. Look at `expression.requiredFields` — ["id","identifier","name","gender","birthDate"]. This is exactly what request #5 below checks a Patient resource against. Try GET .../rules/NOT_A_REAL_CODE afterward — expect 404.

Expect: 200 OK, `allValid: false`. resourceResults has 4 entries — p1 valid:true (has everything), p2 valid:false (missing identifier/name/birthDate — read the `reason` field), m1 valid:true (has medicationReference, satisfying the medication[x] choice), m2 valid:false (missing BOTH medicationCodeableConcept and medicationReference — see how missingFields shows them joined with '|', meaning 'either one would have worked'). validationReportIds has 2 entries (one per failure) — go check `silver.validation_reports` in DBeaver/psql for those ids and you'll see the same reason text persisted there.

item.name: 4. Validate — unsupported resource type is skipped, not failed

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, `allValid: true`, `resourceResults: []`. Practitioner has no USCORE_* rule registered, so it's silently skipped rather than counted as a failure — same 'skip what you don't own' convention as rules-engine-service's RuleExecutor. This is the behavior request #8 below exercises deliberately via a toggle.

item.name: 5. Generate — full patient record, all 7 resource types

request.description: Expect: 200 OK, a FHIR Bundle (`resourceType: "Bundle"`, `type: "collection"`) with 7 entries — one Patient (id patient-901) plus one each of Condition/Observation/MedicationRequest/AllergyIntolerance/Encounter/DiagnosticReport. Note the real terminology system URIs in each `code.coding[0].system` (e.g. http://hl7.org/fhir/sid/icd-10-cm for the Condition). After this call, check `gold.fhir_resources` in psql/DBeaver — you should see all 7 rows with `is_us_core_compliant = true`.

Expect: 200 OK, a Bundle with exactly 1 entry (just the Patient — no name given, so the `name` field is omitted entirely rather than sent as null; look for that). Confirms every item list is genuinely optional.
Expect: 200 OK, the rule object with `active: false`. This takes effect immediately — no restart needed.

item.name: 8. Validate again — toggled-off rule is now skipped

request.description: Run this right after #7. Expect: 200 OK, `allValid: true`, `resourceResults: []` — the SAME incomplete Patient that failed in request #3 is now skipped, because its rule is inactive. This proves the toggle works live. Run request #9 next to restore it before you forget.
Expect: 200 OK, `active: true`. Always run this after #7/#8 so the rule catalog is back to its normal state for anyone testing after you.

Expect: 200 with compliant=false. No meta.profile, so it's checked against us-core-patient automatically. Violations (errors first) include Patient.gender and Patient.identifier (missing — each with a suggestedFix), and Patient.name[0].family (empty string). Send an X-Correlation-Id header to see it echoed back and stamped on the service's log lines.
Expect: 200, compliant=true, errorCount=0. One WARNING (dom-6: no narrative) is a best-practice note, not a failure.

Expect: 200, compliant=true, profile=us-core-observation-lab (picked because category=laboratory). LOINC code existence is a WARNING (no terminology server here — ontology-service owns that check). Change the UCUM code to 'percent' to see a real ERROR.

item.name: 13. HL7 validate — not a FHIR resource

request.description: Expect: 400 {"error":"Invalid FHIR resource", ...}. Only unparseable / non-FHIR payloads get 400; a non-compliant resource is still a 200.

Expect: 200, one result per silver.patients row. Seed patients SEED-0001 and SEED-0002 are fully compliant; SEED-0003 (deliberately bad) has a non-compliant Patient (Patient.name) and Condition (Condition.code). Then in DBeaver: SELECT resource_type, fhir_id, is_us_core_compliant, compliance_notes FROM gold.fhir_resources WHERE fhir_id LIKE 'silver-%'. Re-running is idempotent (upserts, same 18 rows).
Expect: 200 for an existing silver.patients id (3 = the deliberately bad seed patient); 404 for an id that doesn't exist.

request.description: Expect: 200, allCompliant=true, resourceCount=9 (1 Patient, 3 Condition, 2 MedicationRequest, 3 Observation), notes=[]. Check: the response header X-Correlation-Id echoes `ccda-postman-1`; every `bundle.entry[1..].resource.subject.reference` equals the Patient's `fullUrl` (urn:uuid:...); Condition 1 carries both SNOMED 44054006 and ICD-10-CM E11.9 codings with text resolved from the section narrative (#problem1); the bronchitis Condition is `resolved` with an abatement date; MedicationRequest 1 has requester.display `Dr. Henry Seven` and a q12h timing; MedicationRequest 2 (moodCode EVN, no author) has reportedBoolean=true and a data-absent-reason requester; the creatinine Observation inherits the organizer's effectiveTime. WARNINGs about unknown code systems (LOINC/SNOMED/RxNorm/NCI) are expected: there's no terminology server, ontology-service owns code validity. Send it twice: the resource ids are identical (deterministic from the C-CDA entry ids).

request.description: Expect: 200 (non-compliance is reported, not rejected), allCompliant=false, compliantCount=3 of resourceCount=7. Exactly four ERRORs, one per deliberate gap: Patient.gender (no administrativeGenderCode), Condition.code (value nullFlavor=UNK), MedicationRequest.status and Observation.status (no statusCode). Each has a suggestedFix. `notes` lists the three entries the transformer couldn't fully map. The clean entry in each section stays compliant.
Expect: 400 {"error":"Invalid C-CDA document","message":"Not well-formed XML (line N, column M): ..."}.
Expect: 400, message mentions `DOCTYPE declarations are not allowed`. The parser refuses any DOCTYPE outright, so external entities can never resolve (C-CDA never needs a DTD).

item.name: 20. C-CDA → FHIR — XML but not a ClinicalDocument

request.description: Expect: 400, message `Root element must be {urn:hl7-org:v3}ClinicalDocument, found {http://hl7.org/fhir}Patient`.
Expect: 415 Unsupported Media Type. The endpoint accepts application/xml or text/xml only.

item.name: 22. Build one Silver patient → Gold (GoldWriter: master + lineage)

request.description: Expect: 200. Response now includes masterPatientId — the PROVISIONAL 1:1 gold.master_patients row GoldWriter created (first build) or reused (rebuilds) for this Silver patient. In DBeaver: gold.master_patients (match_status = PROVISIONAL), gold.patient_source_xref, and gold.data_lineage (one FHIR_MAP row per resource; transformation_details.steps = SILVER → GOLD with input_hash/output_hash; one PMI_PROVISIONAL row for the master). Run it twice: same masterPatientId, same goldIds, no new lineage rows.

Expect: 200 []. Migration 19 seeds CMS-0057 resources straight into Gold as PENDING_VALIDATION; GoldWriter validates them on startup, so by now nothing is pending. To see it work: UPDATE gold.fhir_resources SET compliance_notes = '{"status":"PENDING_VALIDATION","seed":"19_seed_cms0057_gold.sql"}' WHERE fhir_id = 'cms-practitionerrole-2'; then re-send — one summary back, usCoreCompliant false, rule pd-1.
Expect: 200 searchset Bundle, total 1 (SEED-0001's commercial PPO Coverage). Validated against us-core-coverage.
Expect: 200 application/fhir+json. Response headers: X-Profile-Compliant: true, X-Validated-Profile: us-core-coverage, ETag, Last-Modified.
Expect: 200, total 2. Try also ?active=true&specialty=207Q00000X (AND) → 1, or ?role=207Q00000X,207RC0000X (comma = OR) → 2.
Expect: 200 with X-Profile-Compliant: false. Deliberately seeded with no telecom and no endpoint → US Core pd-1. The reasons are in gold.fhir_resources.compliance_notes.
Expect: 200, total 1 (metformin 500 MG Oral Tablet, SCD + its SCDG). Validated against Da Vinci US Drug Formulary 2.1.0 usdf-FormularyDrug. Try ?status=active&_count=2 → total 3, 2 entries.

Expect: 200, total 1. An unversioned canonical matches any version (the stored one is pinned |0.1.000, as DEQM's deqm-0 requires). Validated against Da Vinci DEQM 5.0.0 indv-measurereport-deqm. Also: ?patient={{seed1_patient}}.

item.name: 30. CMS-0057 — Device by patient and SNOMED type

request.description: Expect: 200, total 1 (SEED-0002's pacemaker). Validated against us-core-implantable-device.
Expect: 404, OperationOutcome issue code not-found.
Expect: 404, OperationOutcome issue code not-supported, listing the 5 supported types.
Expect: 400, OperationOutcome issue code invalid, naming the parameter and listing the supported ones. Strict handling: an ignored filter would return more data than asked for.
Expect: 400 (modifiers not supported). Also try ?patient=Practitioner/cms-practitioner-1 (wrong reference type), ?_count=1000 (cap 100), PractitionerRole?active=yes.
Expect: 200 and the X-Correlation-Id you sent echoed back in the response headers (and stamped on this request's log lines).
